assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational synthesis that reshaped monetary macroeconomics and the analysis of stabilization policy.
assessment.attribution: Calvo, Taylor, and Woodford represent central distinct pillars, though the broader intellectual contribution is unusually crowded.
assessment.maturity: Its theoretical framework and policy relevance have been extensively tested and embedded in central-bank practice.
uncertainties: Separating the central prize-worthy contribution from related work by other listed macroeconomists is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The firm-heterogeneity framework transformed modern trade theory and empirical work on trade gains and adjustment.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is indispensable to the core selection model, with Helpman and Redding major contributors to its development and application.
assessment.maturity: The framework has generated a large, durable literature and clear implications for trade policy and distribution.
uncertainties: The appropriate boundary between this contribution and adjacent trade-policy contributions remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral-based propagation mechanisms supplied a central explanation for how financial conditions amplify macroeconomic fluctuations.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore are central to collateral constraints, while Gertler made foundational contributions to the financial-accelerator formulation.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms have been deeply integrated into macro-finance research and gained salience through major financial crises.
uncertainties: The candidate combines closely related but not identical mechanisms with several plausible claimants.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work made political institutions, state capacity, and fiscal choices central objects of rigorous economic analysis.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson, and Tabellini have complementary and highly visible contributions to the modern political-economy agenda.
assessment.maturity: The research program is long-standing, influential across theory and empirics, and consequential for public policy.
uncertainties: Its breadth makes a sharply delimited discovery harder to state than for more unified methodological contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work provided enduring economic foundations for analyzing exhaustible natural capital, biodiversity, and sustainable development.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are closely identified with the early theoretical foundations of the proposed contribution.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are mature and increasingly important as environmental constraints enter mainstream economic policy analysis.
uncertainties: The broad inclusive-wealth and biodiversity agenda includes substantial contributions beyond these two economists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantifying misallocation gave growth and development research a powerful account of persistent productivity and income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow supplied the landmark empirical-accounting approach, with Restuccia a major architect of the wider research program.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been widely used, debated, and extended across countries and sectors.
uncertainties: Measurement and causal interpretation of inferred wedges remain actively contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods became essential tools for credible empirical analysis when persistence and unobserved heterogeneity coexist.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are directly associated with the core estimator, while Blundell was crucial to its influential extension.
assessment.maturity: The methods are decades old, broadly adopted, and their strengths and limitations are well understood.
uncertainties: Its importance as a widely used estimator may be judged more technical than a broad conceptual economic discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research fundamentally clarified how trade and technology shocks reshape local labour markets, occupations, and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson are the clearest joint claimants for the signature empirical evidence on trade exposure and labour-market adjustment.
assessment.maturity: The findings have accumulated extensive follow-on evidence and substantially changed policy debate.
uncertainties: The relative roles of trade, technology, and institutions in observed labour-market outcomes remain difficult to disentangle.
